title: DO NOT BE AFRAID TO GO DOWN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I am God, the God of your father,' he said. 'Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.'" — Gen 46:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God knows Jacob is afraid, and He says so directly.

And Jacob has good reason to be. His grandfather Abraham had gone down to Egypt during a famine and it had gone badly (Gen 12:10-20). His father Isaac had been specifically told by God *not* to go down to Egypt (Gen 26:2). Egypt is where the promised land is not. Every family instinct says this is the wrong direction.

So God speaks the fear out loud and then addresses it: do not be afraid, for I will make you into a great nation there. *There.* In the very place that looks like a step away from the promise, God will do the promising.

This matters. God's plan does not always run along the route we expect. Sometimes obedience takes us somewhere that feels like the wrong direction entirely — a smaller job, an unfamiliar city, a season that looks like losing ground.

The question is never whether the path looks right. It is whether God is in it. Jacob is not being told Egypt will be easy; his descendants will one day be slaves there. He is being told God will be with him in it.

That is enough, and it is the same assurance we are given (Heb 13:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you afraid of right now that God already knows about?
2. Has God ever led you somewhere that felt like the wrong direction?
3. What is the difference between a path that looks right and a path God is in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know my fears before I name them. Give me courage to follow You even when the direction makes no sense to me, trusting that You are in it. Amen.
